name: Ukit
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page ukit1237 and reference record 552252 (Smith 2017)
sources.note: Classification Austronesian > MP > North Borneo > Sarawakan > Punan > Bukitan > Ukit; no descriptive (grammar/phonology) reference listed; Smith 2017 is tagged 'overview'.

sources.citation: Sellato, Bernard and Antonia Soriente. 2015. The languages and peoples of the Muller Mountains. Wacana 16(2): 339-354.
sources.note: Consonant tables for Aoheng, Kereho, Hovongan and Bukat (BBL = Bukat-Beketan-Lisum cluster, pp.346-348); no Ukit or Bukitan data; the only stress remark is that Seputan has 'strong stress on the penultimate syllable' (p.344). Silent on Ukit.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1913. The Languages of Borneo. Sarawak Museum Journal 1(4): 1-196.
sources.note: Sec. 10 'Ukit and Bakatan' (p.20) gives only localities; Ukit appears as a column in the comparative vocabulary (MS vocabulary by F. W. Page-Turner 1910, bibliography p.47). No remark on Ukit stress; the one 'stress' sentence in the work concerns Ngaju Mantangai (p.14).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2022. Change Request 2022-014: merge Seru [szd] into Ukit [umi]. SIL International.
sources.note: Administrative merge request; cites De Rozario 1963 [1901] (Bailey's Sru wordlist understood by the Ukit) and Glottolog. No linguistic description, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A comprehensive classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. 723 pp.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: First-hand Ukit data (consultants George Siru and March Majole, Sungai Asap, p.17). Sec. 2.4 Punan subgroup pp.111-127 gives PMP-to-Punan sound correspondences (tables 29-31, pp.112-113), Punan internal subgrouping, and vowel notes; no statement about Ukit (or Punan) word stress. Only Ukit-specific phonetic remark: 'In dialects like Ukit and Buket, where ə is found word-finally, it is realized as [ɘ]' (p.126). Stress statements in the dissertation concern Merap, Segai-Modang, Hliboi Bidayuh, and West Kalimantan Malayic only.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian Languages (rev. ed.). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: Ukit mentioned only as a moribund central-Sarawak language (120 speakers, 1981; pp.65-67) and as a witness for PMP *n/*ñ (p.581). Nothing on Ukit stress.

sources.citation: Rensch, Calvin R. 2012. Melanau and the Languages of Central Sarawak. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012-011. Dallas: SIL International. 100 pp.
sources.note: Comparative lexicostatistic/sound-change survey; Ukit forms are second-hand from Ray 1913 (28 citations) and Urquhart 1955 (6). No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the text (grep stress|accent|prominen returned nothing; 'penult' once, about a vowel correspondence in *ikuR, p.~68).
No phonology; cites only Ethnologue, ELP, Glottolog.
